greeting: Good morning, Zuhair. A big day for theory nerds, so grab a coffee and dig in.

lead.headline: OpenAI says its model has disproved the Exponential Time Hypothesis
lead.summary: OpenAI claims one of its models produced a proof, with a Lean formalisation, that refutes the Exponential Time Hypothesis, a long-standing assumption about how hard certain computing problems are. Leading complexity theorists are now checking it, and they stress that their review is not a certification.

stories.headline: Large language models for computational social science
stories.summary: Published in Nature Human Behaviour on 26 October, this paper sets out future research directions for using LLMs in social science, weighing their promise against their limitations.

stories.headline: Lighter deepfake detector matches existing models
stories.summary: A CU Boulder team built a video deepfake detector that performs comparably to current models while needing far less computing power. It was presented at ACM SIGCOMM 2026.

stories.headline: AI framework cuts compute by two-thirds on long tasks
stories.summary: Researchers at Sungkyunkwan University describe two methods that reduce computing costs and improve success on complex virtual tasks. Both were accepted to NeurIPS 2026, with papers on arXiv.

stories.headline: What OpenAI's Exponential Time Hypothesis claim means
stories.summary: Coverage of the claimed AI-generated algorithm explains that it would solve some hard problems faster in theory, overturning a core hardness assumption if it holds up under review.

stories.headline: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to around 60,000 staff
stories.summary: Microsoft has opened a time-limited voluntary exit offer to employees at level 70 and below across the US, Canada, India and the UK, as it pours money into AI infrastructure.

stories.headline: AI-assisted discovery exposes decade-old PHP flaw
stories.summary: Researchers used AI tooling to find a long-standing vulnerability in PHP that could put millions of websites at risk.

stories.headline: Labor pledges $893m to upgrade 25 local roads
stories.summary: Victorian Labor has promised a further $893 million for 25 roads, 19 of them regional, as roads become a key battleground ahead of the 28 November election.

stories.headline: Fears One Nation rhetoric is stirring divides in Victoria's election
stories.summary: Multicultural leaders warn racism is rising as the national migration debate flows into the state campaign.

stories.headline: Neo-Nazi Thomas Sewell pleads guilty over Camp Sovereignty attack
stories.summary: Sewell and three other men pleaded guilty in the County Court to violent disorder over the 2025 incident at the Camp Sovereignty site.

stories.headline: Liberal candidate's husband allegedly assaulted over campaign signs
stories.summary: A 59-year-old man is charged after a confrontation over Liberal signs in Mernda in which Amanda Dow's husband was allegedly assaulted.

stories.headline: Israel faces political gridlock after election
stories.summary: With most votes counted, no clear winner has emerged from Tuesday's national election, and the final tally could take days.

stories.headline: Houthis claim missile strike on Saudi refinery; Egypt shuts independent outlet
stories.summary: The Houthis say they hit Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery, while Egypt ordered Mada Masr closed and briefly detained its editor.
